text: The Offeror must comply with all Limitations on Subcontracting (LOS) requirements, including VAAR subpart 819.70, SBA regulations at 13 CFR part 121 and part 125 (including the non-manufacturer rule and 13 CFR 121.406(b) and 13 CFR 125.6), and any applicable certification requirements (e.g., 852.219-75 or 852.219-76). Compliance with LOS clauses must be asserted by the offeror in the email accompanying their quote. The SDVOSB/VOSB prime contractor must comply with the following subcontracting limitations: (1) For services (except construction), the prime contractor shall not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance (excluding direct costs that are not the principal purpose of the acquisition and are not provided by the SDVOSB/VOSB, such as airline travel, cloud computing, or mass media) to firms that are not VIP-listed SDVOSBs/VOSBs. (2) For supplies or products (other than from a non-manufacturer), the prime contractor shall not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to firms that are not VIP-listed SDVOSBs/VOSBs. (3) For non-manufacturer supplies, the prime contractor shall supply the product of a domestic small business manufacturer or processor unless a waiver under 13 CFR 121.406(b)(5) has been granted. (4) For general construction, the prime contractor shall not pay more than 85% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to firms that are not VIP-listed SDVOSBs/VOSBs. (5) For special trade construction, the prime contractor shall not pay more than 75% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance, excluding the most cost of materials, to firms that are not VIP-listed SDVOSBs/VOSBs. Any work further subcontracted by a first-tier VIP-listed SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractor counts towards the subcontracting limit. For supply or construction contracts, the cost of materials is excluded from subcontracting calculations. When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50% limitation applies to the service portion or the supply portion, specifically the portion with the preponderance of the expenditure upon which the assigned NAICS is based. Compliance must be met by the end of the base term and each subsequent option period, or by the end of the performance period for each order. A VOSB/SDVOSB must meet the NAICS size standard assigned to the prime and be listed in the VIP system to be considered similarly situated.
